correctness.rationale: The ordinary Veronese polar vector follows from the standard smooth polar-class formula after substituting c_j(TP^n)=binom(n+1,j)h^j and H=e h. Reindexing the closed vector as a_k=binom(N,k)e^(k-1)(e-1)^(N-k), the p-adic proof is exact: for p not dividing e, the endpoint a_N has valuation zero; for p dividing e, binom(N,k)=N/k*binom(N-1,k-1) gives nu_p(binomial)>=nu_p(N)-nu_p(k), and nu_p(k)<=k-1<=(k-1)nu_p(e). Thus every term has valuation at least nu_p(N), while k=1 attains equality. The bundled checker independently verifies the Chern-sum formula, gcd law, and ED-degree sum in large finite ranges.

value.rationale: Polar degrees simultaneously encode the generic tangency conditions represented by all coisotropic hypersurfaces of a projective variety. The theorem determines the exact universal divisibility shared by every one of these degrees for every Veronese embedding: common primes are controlled solely by the overlap between the embedding degree e and n+1, with exact exponents. This is a natural whole-vector arithmetic invariant that is not visible from isolated polar degrees and immediately decides when the complete polar vector is primitive.
